title: Topological enhancements and ideal subsheaves for formal open descent
statement: For the ringed-space formal spectra and finite-cover convention of [def-per-adic-formal-geometry], use the inverse-limit formal section topology of [def-per-adic-principal-chart-data]. A section topology assigns a topology to every structure-sheaf section ring. It is a sheaf of topological rings when operations and restrictions are continuous and the topology on sections of any open is the initial topology for restrictions to a covering family. A formal morphism is a ringed-space morphism continuous on all section rings and local on stalks. A formal open immersion is an underlying open immersion and is a homeomorphism on section rings for opens in its image. An adic space has local rings and is locally isomorphic in this sense to complete adic formal spectra. A Noetherian adic space additionally satisfies the recorded finite formal-affine-cover predicate and has such charts with Noetherian coordinate rings and finitely generated ideals of definition. An ideal subsheaf assigns an ideal to each section ring, stable under restriction, with membership local for covers. Its stalk is the union of the neighborhood ideal images. It is coherent when locally finitely many sections generate its stalk ideals; on Noetherian formal affines this is the completed-localization sheaf of a finitely generated ideal. It is open when locally on formal affine charts its section ideal is open, and is an ideal of definition when locally this open ideal has powers generating the section topology. Pullback along an open immersion is equality after extending stalk ideals. An open cover is a jointly surjective family of formal open immersions. Compatibility of maps or ideals means their pullbacks agree on every common overlap. Cover descent means unique gluing of continuous local maps, locality of their equality, and unique gluing of coherent ideal subsheaves, preserving openness and the ideal-of-definition condition. Stable descent requires every open subspace to remain Noetherian adic and every cover of it to satisfy cover descent. A finite formal gluing datum enhances the usual ringed-space gluing datum by these section topologies and continuous local transition maps, with Noetherian adic pieces. A realization is a Noetherian adic space covered by the pieces, with the transition identities and cartesian overlap squares.
